title: What Happens When You Get a Charley Horse?
sources: NHS, 'Leg cramps' (leg cramps happen when a muscle in the leg tightens and causes a sudden pain that can make it hard to move; common and usually harmless; most often the calf muscle; cramps can last from a few seconds to 10 minutes; they can happen at any time, but most people have them at night or when resting; stretching and massaging the muscle may ease the pain during a cramp, and putting your weight on the leg with the cramp may also help; after the cramp has stopped the muscle might feel sore for up to 24 hours; see a GP if cramps disturb your sleep, you also have numbness or swelling in your legs, or cramps last longer than 10 minutes): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/leg-cramps/

Cleveland Clinic, 'Muscle Spasms' (muscle spasms, also called muscle cramps, occur when your muscle involuntarily and forcibly contracts and can't relax; charley horses are a common type; contributors include muscle fatigue, not enough stretching and dehydration; a particularly painful cramp can leave lingering discomfort for a day or two; self-care: stretch, massage, heat or ice; see a provider if spasms are unbearably painful, happen frequently or last a long time): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/21190-muscle-cramps

Cleveland Clinic, 'Leg Cramps at Night' (leg cramps are sudden, involuntary, intense muscle spasms, usually in the calf, foot or thigh, also known as charley horses): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/14170-leg-cramps-at-night

Mayo Clinic, 'Muscle cramp' (a sudden, unexpected tightening of one or more muscles; mostly in leg muscles, most often the calf; usually lasts seconds to minutes; the area might be sore for hours or days after; see a provider if cramps cause severe discomfort, come with leg swelling, redness or skin changes, or muscle weakness, happen often, or don't improve with self-care): https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/muscle-cramp/symptoms-causes/syc-20350820 (text verified via the Mayo Clinic Care Network health library mirror)

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Lacrimal Apparatus' (tears drain into your tear ducts, which empty into the back of your nose; when you cry, excess tears flow faster than usual into the back of your nose and drain into your throat, which is why you might feel stuffy): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/24415-lacrimal-apparatus

lines.text: What happens when you get a charley horse?
Your calf clenches tight by itself, sometimes for ten minutes.
lines.caps: YOUR *CALF CLENCHES | TIGHT BY *ITSELF | *SOMETIMES FOR | *10 MINUTES

lines.text: The muscle squeezes on its own and just can't relax,
lines.caps: THE *MUSCLE SQUEEZES | ON ITS *OWN | AND JUST CAN'T *RELAX

lines.text: and the sudden pain can make it hard to move.
lines.caps: AND THE *SUDDEN | *PAIN CAN | MAKE IT *HARD | TO *MOVE

lines.text: Tired muscles and dehydration can trigger it.
Weirdly, most people get them at night, or while resting.
lines.caps: *WEIRDLY, MOST | PEOPLE *GET THEM | AT *NIGHT | OR WHILE *RESTING

lines.text: To fight back, stretch and massage the calf,
or stand up and put your weight on that leg.
lines.caps: OR *STAND UP AND | PUT YOUR *WEIGHT | ON THAT *LEG

lines.text: The calf might stay sore for a day or two.
lines.caps: THE *CALF MIGHT | STAY *SORE | FOR A *DAY | OR *TWO

lines.text: Frequent cramps, swelling or numbness? See a doctor.
